name: Camulos

attributes.attribute: name used in the town of Camulodunum
linked Camulos with their war god Mars

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Camulos held great power in early Britain and in Gaul. The Belgae and the Remi gave him special honour. The Romans saw a warrior in him and tied him to Mars. A stone at Rindern carries the name Mars-Camulo under an oak crown. Some carvings give him a ram-horned head. His fame shows in many place names. Camulodunum keeps his memory and later grew into the city of Colchester. A few writers tried to link him to Old King Cole and to the hero Fionn's father. Modern scholars reject those claims. The hard evidence does not hold for such a link. His true standing rests on the stones and the town name.

okr.objective: Camulos is a thinly attested British god.
key_results: Only a little evidence of his cult survives.
His name lives on in the town name Camulodunum.
Camulodunum means “fort of Camulos” and became Colchester.
The Romans tied him to their war god Mars.
Scholars link him with the Irish ancestor Cumhall.
